exposure: SUPREME laryngeal mask airway (SLMA) in emergency cesarean delivery under general anesthesia (GA)
Emergency cesarean delivery under general anesthesia with SUPREME laryngeal mask airway (SLMA)
emergency cesarean delivery under endotracheal intubation
outcome: Incidence of adverse events related to using SLMA
Neonatal outcomes (5-min Apgar score, need for endotracheal intubation)
cohort: 1039 parturients undergoing emergency cesarean delivery under general anesthesia with SLMA
finding: This retrospective study showed that the SLMA was used successfully in 1039 patients undergoing emergent cesarean delivery without any major complications.
mod_finding: This study investigated the use of SLMA during emergency cesarean deliveries, finding it to be a safe and effective alternative to endotracheal intubation.
